questions.stem: What makes a playbook appear for a Security Incident if using Flow Designer?

options.text: Trigger set to conditions that match the security incident

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Playbooks > Trigger Condition: A playbook appears for a Security Incident when the Flow Designer trigger is set to conditions that match the security incident (B). Per p2367: 'This playbook is triggered and associated with the security incident when the security incident is created or updated based on your required conditions.' Actions (A), Runbook property (C), and Service Criticality (D) do not control playbook appearance.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of Calculator Groups as opposed to Calculators?

options.text: To provide metadata about the calculators
To allow the agent to select which calculator they want to execute
To set the condition for all calculators to run
To ensure one at maximum will run per group

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Calculators > Calculator Groups Purpose: Calculator Groups ensure that only one calculator at maximum will run per group (D). When multiple calculators are in a group, the system evaluates conditions and executes only the first matching calculator, preventing conflicting updates. Calculator Groups are not for metadata (A), agent selection (B), or running all calculators simultaneously (C).

questions.stem: The following term is used to describe any observable occurrence: __________.
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Terminology > Observable Occurrence: An Event (E) is the term used to describe any observable occurrence in a system or network. Per NIST SP 800-61 (the standard underlying SIR): 'An event is any observable occurrence in a system or network.' An Alert (D) is generated when events match predefined rules and require investigation. Incident (A) is a broader response record. Log (B) is raw recorded data. Ticket (C) is a work tracking record.

questions.stem: The severity field of the security incident is influenced by what?

options.text: The cost of the response to the security breach
The impact, urgency and priority of the incident
The time taken to resolve the security incident
The business value of the affected asset

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Incidents > Severity Influences: The severity field of a security incident is influenced by the impact, urgency, and priority of the incident (B). Per p1911/p1914, severity calculators evaluate Risk Score which is derived from Business Impact and Priority fields. The cost of response (A) and time to resolve (C) are outcomes, not severity drivers. Asset business value (D) may be a calculator input but is not the primary stated influence.

questions.stem: The Risk Score is calculated by combining all the weights using __________.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Risk Score > Calculation Method: The Risk Score is calculated by combining all weights using an arithmetic mean (A). Per p1914: 'Security Incident Business Impact weight of 60 + Priority weight of 40 / 2 = a risk score of 50.' This is a standard arithmetic mean (sum divided by count). Addition alone (B) would not normalize the result. Risk Score script include (C) is an implementation detail. Geometric mean (D) is not used.

questions.stem: What are two of the audiences identified that will need reports and insight into Security Incident Response reports? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Reporting > Audiences: Two audiences for Security Incident Response reports are Analysts (A) and the Chief Information Security Officer/CISO (C). Per p1887/p2111, the CISO has a dedicated dashboard role [sn_si.ciso] and analysts need operational metrics to manage workloads. Vulnerability Managers (B) focus on VR reporting. Problem Managers (D) are ITSM-focused and are not a primary SIR audience.

questions.stem: What three steps enable you to include a new playbook in the Selected Playbook choice list? (Choose three.)

options.text: Add the TLP: GREEN tag to the playbooks that you want to include in the Selected Playbook choice list
Search for the new playbook you have created using Flow Designer
Add the sir_playbook tag to the playbooks that you want to include in the Selected Playbook choice list

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Playbooks > Adding to Choice List: Three steps to include a new playbook in the Selected Playbook choice list are: navigate to the sys_hub_flow.list table (B), search for the new playbook created in Flow Designer (C), and add the sir_playbook tag to the playbook (D). Per p1934: 'Navigate to sys_hub_flow.list... Search for the new playbook... add the sir_playbook tag.' TLP:GREEN tag (A) and sys_playbook_flow.list (E) are not the correct steps.

questions.stem: Which improvement opportunity can be found baseline which can contribute towards process maturity and strengthen costumer’s overall security posture?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Process Improvement > Post-Incident Review: Post-Incident Review (A) is the baseline improvement opportunity that contributes towards process maturity and strengthens security posture. Reviewing incidents after resolution identifies gaps, root causes, and areas for improvement in the response process. Fast Eradication (B), Containment (C), and Analysis (D) are operational phases, not process improvement mechanisms.

questions.stem: What is the fastest way for security incident administrators to remove unwanted widgets from the Security Incident Catalog?

options.text: Clicking the X on the top right corner

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Incident Catalog > Widget Removal: The fastest way for security incident administrators to remove unwanted widgets from the Security Incident Catalog is through the Catalog Definition record (D). The Catalog Definition record controls which widgets appear in the catalog view. Clicking X (A) is not an option on catalog widgets. System administrator involvement (B) is unnecessary. Widgets can be removed (C is incorrect).

questions.stem: Select the one capability that retrieves a list of running processes on a CI from a host or endpoint.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Capabilities > Get Running Processes: Get Running Processes (C) retrieves a list of running processes from a CI/host/endpoint. Per p4291: 'Get Running Processes: Retrieves a list of running processes from an endpoint or host. This capability is used for incident enrichment during investigations.' Get Network Statistics (A) retrieves network connections. Isolate Host (B) isolates an endpoint. Publish Watchlist (D) and Block Action (E) are different capabilities.

questions.stem: Which Table would be commonly used for Security Incident Response?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Tables > Security Incident Table: The table commonly used for Security Incident Response is sn_si_incident (D). Per p2053: 'Table: Security Incident (sn_si_incident)' is used for response templates and quick messages in SIR. sysapproval_approver (A) is for approvals. sec_ops_incident (B) is not a standard SIR table name. cmdb_rel_ci (C) is for CMDB CI relationships.

questions.stem: There are several methods in which security incidents can be raised, which broadly fit into one of these categories: __________. (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Incident Creation > Categories: Security incidents broadly fall into two creation categories: manually created (B) and automatically created (C). Manual creation includes analysts directly entering incidents. Automatic creation includes alert rules, integrations, and email parsing. Integrations (A) and email parsing (D) are specific methods within the automatic category, not separate high-level categories.

questions.stem: What is the first step when creating a security Playbook?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Playbooks > Creation First Step: The first step when creating a security playbook is to create a Flow (B) in Flow Designer. Playbooks in SIR are built as flows in Flow Designer with triggers and actions. Creating a Runbook (C) is a separate feature for knowledge article associations. Response Task state (A) and Knowledge Article (D) are later configuration steps, not the first step in playbook creation.

questions.stem: To configure Security Incident Escalations, you need the following role(s): __________.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Escalations > Required Role: The sn_si.admin role (A) is required to configure Security Incident Escalations. Per p1885, sn_si.admin has 'Full control over all Security Incident Response data' including administrative configurations like escalations. sn_si.manager (in B/D) can manage incidents but lacks escalation configuration access. sn_si.ciso (C) has dashboard access but not configuration rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following are potential benefits for utilizing Security Incident assignment automation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Assignment Automation > Benefits: Two benefits of Security Incident assignment automation are Decreased Time to Containment (A) and Increased resolution process consistency (D). Automated assignment routes incidents to the right analyst faster, reducing containment time. Consistent rule-based routing improves process standardization. Increased Mean Time to Remediation (B) would be a negative outcome. Decreased Time to Ingestion (C) relates to alert ingestion, not assignment.

questions.stem: What is the key to a successful implementation?

options.text: Sell customer the most expensive package
Understanding the customer’s goals and objectives

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Implementation > Success Key: The key to a successful implementation is understanding the customer's goals and objectives (C). A successful SIR implementation requires aligning the solution to actual business outcomes and security requirements. Selling the most expensive package (A), implementing everything (B), and building custom integrations (D) do not ensure success without customer goal alignment.

questions.stem: A flow consists of one or more actions and a what?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Flow Components: A flow consists of one or more actions and a Trigger (D). In ServiceNow Flow Designer, a flow is defined by its trigger (the event that initiates the flow) and one or more actions (the steps to execute). Change formatter (A) is a UI element. Catalog Designer (B) is for service catalog. NIST Ready State (C) is not a flow component.

questions.stem: Flow Triggers can be based on what? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Trigger Types: Flow triggers can be based on Record changes (A), Schedules (B), and Record inserts (D). These are the three primary Flow Designer trigger types for SIR automation. Subflows (C) are reusable flow components called from within flows — they are not triggers. Record views (E) do not trigger flows in ServiceNow Flow Designer.

questions.stem: Which one of the following users is automatically added to the Request Assessments list?

options.text: Any user that adds a worknote to the ticket
The analyst assigned to the ticket
Any user who has Response Tasks on the incident
The Affected User on the incident

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Assessments > Auto-Added Users: Any user who has Response Tasks on the security incident is automatically added to the Request Assessments list (C). Response task assignees are involved in the incident and should receive assessment requests. Worknote authors (A) are not automatically added. The assigned analyst (B) may or may not have response tasks. The Affected User (D) is the subject of the incident, not necessarily an assessor.

questions.stem: For Customers who don't use 3rd-party systems, what ways can security incidents be created? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Incident Creation > Non-3rd-Party Methods: For customers not using 3rd-party systems, three ways to create security incidents are: Security Service Catalog (A), Security Incident Form (B), and Inbound Email Parsing Rules (C). Per p1871: 'From the Security Incident form... From the service catalog.' Email parsing is a native ServiceNow capability. Leveraging an Integration (D) and Alert Management (E) require 3rd-party system connections.

questions.stem: What does a flow require?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Flow Requirements: A flow requires a trigger (D) to initiate execution. In ServiceNow Flow Designer, every flow must have a trigger that defines when the flow runs — such as record changes, scheduled times, or record inserts. Security orchestration flows (A) are a type of flow, not a requirement. Runbooks (B) and CAB orders (C) are separate SIR and ITSM constructs unrelated to flow requirements.

questions.stem: Knowledge articles that describe steps an analyst needs to follow to complete Security incident tasks might be associated to those tasks through which of the following?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Runbooks > Knowledge Article Association: Knowledge articles describing steps for security incident tasks are associated to those tasks through a Runbook (D). Per p2220: 'You can organize knowledge articles into runbooks, which create associations between the articles and specific tasks.' A runbook automatically opens a relevant knowledge article when an analyst is working on a matched task. Work Instruction Playbook (A), Flow (B), and Workflow (C) do not create this article-to-task association.

questions.stem: Which of the following process definitions allow only single-step progress through the process defined without allowing step skipping?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Process Definitions > NIST Stateful: NIST Stateful (B) is the process definition that allows only single-step progress without step skipping. Per p1899, NIST Stateful enforces strict sequential state transitions — analysts must complete each step before advancing. NIST Open (D) allows step skipping. SANS Open (C) follows the open SANS framework allowing flexible progression. SANS Stateful (A) is not a provided process definition.

questions.stem: If the customer’s email server currently has an account setup to report suspicious emails, then what happens next?

options.text: an integration added to Exchange keeps the ServiceNow platform in sync
the ServiceNow platform ensures that parsing and analysis takes place on their mail server
the customer’s systems are already handling suspicious emails
the customer should set up a rule to forward these mails onto the ServiceNow platform

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Email Phishing > Forwarding Setup: If the customer's email server has an account to report suspicious emails, the next step is to set up a rule to forward those emails to the ServiceNow platform (D). ServiceNow receives the forwarded emails through its inbound email parsing capabilities to create security incidents. An Exchange integration (A) keeps systems in sync but isn't the next step. Email analysis stays on the ServiceNow side (B is incorrect). Handling only externally (C) misses the SIR workflow.

questions.stem: What parts of the Security Incident Response lifecycle is responsible for limiting the impact of a security incident?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Incident Lifecycle > Impact Limitation: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery (D) is the lifecycle phase responsible for limiting the impact of a security incident. Containment stops the spread, eradication removes the threat, and recovery restores normal operations. Post Incident Activity (A) occurs after resolution. Detection & Analysis (B) identifies the threat. Preparation and Identification (C) is before active response.

questions.stem: Select the one capability that restricts connections from one CI to other devices.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Capabilities > Isolate Host: Isolate Host (A) is the capability that restricts connections from one CI to other devices. Per p4291: 'Isolate Host: Provides a way to isolate an endpoint or a host associated with a security incident.' Per p2042: 'Isolate Host: This capability restricts...' Sightings Search (B) and Get Network Statistics (E) are investigative. Block Action (C) blocks specific traffic. Get Running Processes (D) retrieves process lists.

questions.stem: What factor, if any, limits the ability to close SIR records?

options.text: Best practice dictates that SIR records should be set to 'Resolved' never to 'Closed'
Nothing, SIR records could be closed at any time
All post-incident review questioners have to be completed first

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Closing Records > Blocking Factors: All post-incident review questionnaires (assessments) must be completed before a SIR record can be closed (D). Per p1970, closing is blocked when there are 'pending activities such as active tasks, playbooks, child SIs, assessments, or active flows.' Post-incident assessments/questionnaires are the specific review completion requirement. Open INC records (A) do not block SIR closure. SIR records can be fully closed (B is incorrect). Nothing blocking (C) is incorrect.

questions.stem: When the Security Phishing Email record is created what types of observables are stored in the record? (Choose three.)

options.text: URLs, domains, or IP addresses appearing in the body
Hashes and/or file names found in the EML attachment
Type of Ingestion Rule used to identify this email as a phishing attempt

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Phishing Email > Stored Observables: Three types of observables stored in a Security Phishing Email record are: URLs, domains, or IP addresses from the email body (A); IP addresses from the email header (D); and hashes and/or file names from the EML attachment (E). Per p2143/p2136, these are the observable types automatically extracted during phishing analysis. Who reported (B), State (C), and Ingestion Rule type (F) are metadata, not observables.

questions.stem: What plugin must be activated to see the New Security Analyst UI?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Analyst Workspace > Required Plugin: The Security Incident Response UI plugin (B) must be activated to see the new Security Analyst UI. This plugin installs the Security Analyst Workspace and all associated new UI components. Security Analyst UI Plugin (A), Security Operations UI plugin (C), and Security Agent UI Plugin (D) are not the correct plugin names for activating the SIR analyst workspace.

questions.stem: The benefits of improved Security Incident Response are expressed __________.

options.text: as desirable outcomes with clear, measurable Key Performance Indicators
differently depending upon 3 stages: Process Improvement, Process Design, and Post Go-Live
as a series of states with consistent, clear metrics
as a value on a scale of 1-10 based on specific outcomes

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Benefits > Expression Format: The benefits of improved Security Incident Response are expressed as desirable outcomes with clear, measurable Key Performance Indicators (A). KPIs such as Mean Time to Respond, Time to Containment, and incident closure rates provide measurable evidence of improvement. The other options describe implementation stages (B), state metrics (C), or a numerical scale (D) that are not the standard way SIR benefits are expressed.

questions.stem: This type of integration workflow helps retrieve a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint, so it can be used to enrich incidents during investigation.

options.text: Security Incident Response – Get Running Services
Security Incident Response – Get Network Statistics

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Capabilities > Get Network Statistics: The Security Incident Response – Get Network Statistics (B) workflow retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint for incident enrichment during investigation. Per p4291: 'Get Network Statistics: Retrieves a list of active network connections from an endpoint or host. This capability is used for incident enrichment.' Get Running Services (A) is not a standard capability name. Sightings Search (C) finds occurrences of observables. Block Request (D) is a blocking action.

questions.stem:
Joe is on the SIR Team and needs to be able to configure Territories and Skills.
What role does he need?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Roles > Territories and Skills: The Security Admin role [sn_si.admin] (D) is required to configure Territories and Skills. Per p1885: 'Security Incident Administrator [sn_si.admin] - Full control over all Security Incident Response data. Also administers territories and skills, as needed.' Security Basic (A), Manager (B), and Analyst (C) roles do not include territory and skills administration rights.

questions.stem: Why should discussions focus with the end in mind?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Implementation > End in Mind: Discussions should focus with the end in mind to understand desired outcomes (A). Starting with the desired end state ensures that implementation decisions are aligned to business goals and measurable success criteria. Understanding current posture (B), process (C), and tools (D) are supporting activities, but the primary reason for an 'end in mind' focus is to define and target the desired outcomes.

questions.stem: Which of the following State Flows are provided for Security Incidents? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Process Definitions > State Flow Types: Three state flows provided for Security Incidents are NIST Open (A), SANS Open (B), and NIST Stateful (C). Per p1899, NIST supports NIST Stateful and NIST Open. SANS provides SANS Open. SANS Stateful (D) is not a provided process definition in the base system — SANS only provides the Open model in ServiceNow SIR.

questions.stem: Chief factors when configuring auto-assignment of Security Incidents are __________.

options.text: Agent group membership, Agent location and time zone
Security incident priority, CI Location and agent time zone
Agent skills, System Schedules and agent location
Agent location, Agent skills and agent time zone

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Auto-Assignment > Chief Factors: The chief factors when configuring auto-assignment of Security Incidents are Agent location, Agent skills, and agent time zone (D). Per p1893/p2172/p2173, Advanced Work Assignment considers skills match, geographic proximity (location), and time zone alignment when selecting the best agent. Security incident priority (B) and CI location (B) are not among the primary AWA selection factors.

questions.stem: Which ServiceNow automation capability extends Flow Designer to integrate business processes with other systems?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Integration Capability: Integration Hub (D) is the ServiceNow automation capability that extends Flow Designer to integrate business processes with other systems. Integration Hub provides spokes — pre-built connectors to third-party systems like SIEM platforms, EDR tools, and ticketing systems. Workflow (A) is the legacy automation engine. Orchestration (B) is server-side automation. Subflows (C) are reusable flow components within Flow Designer.

questions.stem: In order to see the Actions in Flow Designer for Security Incident, what plugin must be activated?

options.text: Performance Analytics for Security Incident Response

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Security Actions Plugin: The Security Operations Spoke (C) plugin must be activated to see Security Incident actions in Flow Designer. The Security Operations Spoke provides spoke actions for SIR workflows including incident enrichment, capability execution, and observable management. Performance Analytics (A) is for reporting. Security Spoke (B) is not the precise name. Security Incident Spoke (D) is not a plugin name.

questions.stem: How do you select which process definition to use?

options.text: By selecting the desired process within the Process Definition module
By selecting the desired process within the Process Selection module
By setting the process definition record to Active
By setting the Script Include record to Active

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Process Definitions > Selection Method: To select which process definition to use, navigate to the Process Selection module (B). Per p1900: 'Navigate to All > Security Incident Response > Administration > Process Selection. Click the search icon to list the available process definitions. Select a process definition. Click Update.' The Process Definition module (A) is for creating/editing definitions, not selecting one. Activating records (C, D) alone does not select the active process.

questions.stem: What role(s) are required to add new items to the Security Incident Catalog?

options.text: requires both sn_si.write and catalog_admin roles

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Incident Catalog > Required Role: Adding new items to the Security Incident Catalog requires the sn_si.admin role (A). The security admin has full control over all Security Incident Response data and configurations including the catalog. sn_si.catalog (B) is not a standard SIR role. sn_si.write + catalog_admin (C) is not the stated requirement. Admin alone (D) is not the minimum SIR-specific role required.

questions.stem: What is calculated as an arithmetic mean taking into consideration different values in the CI, Security Incident, and User records?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Risk Score > Arithmetic Mean Calculation: Risk Score (D) is calculated as an arithmetic mean taking into consideration different values in the CI, Security Incident, and User records. Per p1914: weights from Business Impact and Priority are averaged — e.g., (60+40)/2 = 50. Calculators incorporate CI criticality, user criticality, and security incident data to derive the final score. Priority (A), Business Impact (B), and Severity (C) are inputs to the Risk Score, not the arithmetic mean calculation result.

questions.stem: What is the name of the Inbound Action that validates whether an inbound email should be processed as a phishing email for URP v2?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > User Reported Phishing > Inbound Action: The 'Create Phishing Email' inbound action (D) validates whether an inbound email should be processed as a phishing email for URP v2. Per p2141: 'The Create Phishing Email inbound action runs on the email record' to create a Phishing Email record in the sn_si_phishing_email table. User Reporting Phishing inbound actions (A, C) were available prior to SIR 9.0 but are now disabled. Scan email (B) is not the inbound action name.

questions.stem: When a record is created in the Security Incident Phishing Email table what is triggered to create a Security Incident?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > User Reported Phishing > Security Incident Creation: When a phishing email record is created, the Transform flow (B) is triggered to create a Security Incident. Per p2138: 'The Transform user-reported phishing emails to security incidents flow creates security incidents from the phishing email records and aggregates similar records into a single incident.' Ingestion Rules (A) match emails to create phishing records. Transform workflow (C) is the legacy approach. Duplication Rule (D) is for aggregation logic.

questions.stem: If a desired pre-built integration cannot be found in the platform, what should be your next step to find a certified integration?

options.text: Build your own through the REST API Explorer
Ask for assistance in the community page
Look for one in the ServiceNow Store

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Integrations > Finding Certified Integrations: If a desired pre-built integration cannot be found in the platform, the next step is to look for one in the ServiceNow Store (D). The ServiceNow Store hosts certified, partner-developed integrations for SIR and other applications. Building via REST API Explorer (A) is a last resort. Community page (B) is for support, not downloads. ServiceNow Share (C) hosts community contributions, not certified integrations.

questions.stem:
Incident severity is influenced by the business value of the affected asset.
Which of the following are asset types that can be affected by an incident? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Severity Calculators > Asset Types: Two asset types that can be affected by an incident (influencing severity) are Business Service (A) and Configuration Item (B). Per p1909: 'If the configuration item in the security incident is associated with a highly critical business service, the Risk score, Business Impact, and Priority fields are elevated.' Calculator Group (C) and Severity Calculator (D) are configuration tools, not asset types.

questions.stem: A pre-planned response process contains which sequence of events?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Pre-planned Response > Sequence: A pre-planned response process contains the sequence: Organize, Analyze, Prioritize, Contain (A). This sequence reflects the structured workflow of organizing the response team, analyzing the incident, prioritizing based on risk, and containing the threat. The other options substitute Analyze with Detect (B), Prepare (C), or Verify (D), which do not match the standard pre-planned response sequence.

questions.stem: Why is it important that the Platform (System) Administrator and the Security Incident administrator role be separated? (Choose three.)

options.text: Access to security incident data may need to be restricted
Allow SIR Teams to control assignment of security roles
Reduce the number of incidents assigned to the Platform Admin
Preserve the security image in the company

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Role Separation > Reasons: Three reasons to separate Platform Admin and Security Incident admin roles are: access to SIR data may need to be restricted (A), allow SIR teams to control assignment of security roles (B), and clear separation of duty (C). Per p1885: 'Security Incident Response can be restricted from the administrator.' This ensures data privacy, appropriate access control, and governance compliance. Reducing incident count (D) and preserving security image (E) are not architectural separation reasons.

questions.stem: Using the KB articles for Playbooks tasks also gives you which of these advantages?

options.text: Automated activities to run scans and enrich Security Incidents with real time data
Automated activities to resolve security Incidents through patching
Improved visibility to threats and vulnerabilities
Enhanced ability to create and present concise, descriptive tasks

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Runbooks > KB Article Advantage: Using KB articles for Playbook tasks provides the enhanced ability to create and present concise, descriptive tasks (D). KB articles provide rich contextual instructions for each task in the playbook, making task descriptions more informative and actionable for analysts. Automated scans/enrichment (A) and automated patching (B) are capability functions. Improved visibility (C) is a general SIR benefit, not specific to KB articles for playbooks.

questions.stem: The EmailUserReportedPhishing script include processes inbound emails and creates a record in which table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Phishing Email > Table: The EmailUserReportedPhishing script include processes inbound emails and creates a record in the sn_si_phishing_email table (D). Per p2141/p2138, phishing email records are stored in sn_si_phishing_email. These records are then processed by the Transform flow to create security incidents (sn_si_incident). ar_sn_si_phishing_email (A), sn_si_incident (B), and sn_si_phishing_email_header (C) are not where the phishing email record is first created.

questions.stem: A flow consists of __________. (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Flow Components: A flow consists of Actions (B) and Triggers (E). In ServiceNow Flow Designer, a trigger defines when the flow runs, and actions define what the flow does. Scripts (A) may be used within actions but are not a primary flow component. Processes (C) and Actors (D) are not standard Flow Designer component types.

questions.stem: Which of the following process definitions are not provided baseline?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Process Definitions > Not Baseline: SANS Stateful (B) is NOT provided as a baseline process definition. Per p1899, the baseline process definitions are NIST Stateful, NIST Open, and SANS Open. NIST supports two models (Stateful and Open); SANS only provides the Open model. A SANS Stateful variant does not exist in the ServiceNow base system.

questions.stem: Which of the following tag classifications are provided baseline? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Tags > Baseline Classifications: Three baseline tag classifications provided are Traffic Light Protocol (A), Block from Sharing (B), and Enrichment whitelist/blacklist (G). Per p4273, Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) is a built-in tag group for controlling information sharing. Block from Sharing and Enrichment whitelist/blacklist are also baseline tag groups for observable management. IoC Type (C), Severity (D), Cyber Kill Chain Step (E), and Escalation Level (F) are not baseline tag classifications.

questions.stem:
David is on the Network team and has been assigned a security incident response task.
What role does he need to be able to view and work the task?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Roles > Response Task Access: David needs the Security Analyst role [sn_si.analyst] (A) to view and work a security incident response task. The Security Analyst role provides access to work on security incidents and their associated response tasks. Security Basic (B) is read-only access. External (C) is for external users with limited scope. Read (D) provides view-only access without the ability to work tasks.

questions.stem: When a service desk agent uses the Create Security Incident UI action from a regular incident, what occurs?

options.text: The incident is marked resolved with an automatic security resolution code
A security incident is raised on their behalf but only a notification is displayed
A security incident is raised on their behalf and displayed to the service desk agent
The service desk agent is redirected to the Security Incident Catalog to complete the record producer

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > UI Actions > Create Security Incident: When a service desk agent uses the 'Create Security Incident' UI action from a regular incident, a security incident is raised on their behalf but only a notification is displayed (B). Service desk agents have limited SIR access and cannot view the full security incident form. A is incorrect — the INC is not automatically resolved. C incorrectly implies full SIR form display. D is incorrect — the agent is not redirected to the catalog.

questions.stem: Which of the following fields is used to identify an Event that is to be used for Security purposes?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Events > Security Classification Field: The Classification field (B) is used to identify an Event that is to be used for Security purposes. In ServiceNow Event Management, the Classification field on event records categorizes events by their purpose or domain, including security classification. IT (A) is a domain, not a field. Security (C) may be a value but is not the field name. CI (D) is the Configuration Item reference field.

questions.stem: What specific role is required in order to use the REST API Explorer?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > REST API Explorer > Required Role: The rest_api_explorer role (C) is required to use the REST API Explorer. This is a standard ServiceNow platform role specifically for the REST API Explorer tool, which allows users to build and test REST API calls. admin (A) has access but is not the minimum required role. sn_si.admin (B) is SIR-specific and does not grant REST API Explorer access by itself. security_admin (D) is not a standard ServiceNow role name.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an action provided by the Security Incident Response application?

options.text: Create Record on Security Incident state V1
Create Response Task set Incident state V1
Look Up Record on Security Incident state V1

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Flow Designer Actions > SIR Actions: 'Create Response Task set Incident state V1' (C) is an action provided by the Security Incident Response application in Flow Designer. This action creates response tasks and updates the security incident state as part of automated playbook flows. Create Outage (A) is an ITSM action. Create Record on Security Incident (B) and Look Up Record on Security Incident (D) are not standard SIR action names.

questions.stem: Which one of the following reasons best describes why roles for Security Incident Response (SIR) begin with "sn_si"?

options.text: Because SIR is a scoped application, roles and script includes will begin with the sn_si prefix
Because the Security Incident Response application uses a Secure Identity token
Because ServiceNow checks the instance for a Secure Identity when logging on to this scoped application
Because ServiceNow tracks license use against the Security Incident Response Application

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Scoped Application > Role Prefix: SIR roles begin with 'sn_si' because SIR is a scoped application (A). In ServiceNow, scoped applications prefix their artifacts — including roles, tables, and script includes — with the application scope identifier. For Security Incident Response, the scope is 'sn_si'. This is standard scoped app behavior, not a Secure Identity token (B, C) or license tracking mechanism (D).

questions.stem: A Post Incident Review can contain which of the following? (Choose three.)

options.text: Attachments associated with the security incident

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Post Incident Review > Contents: Three items a Post Incident Review can contain are post incident questionnaires (A), an audit trail (B), and Performance Analytics reports (E). Per p2223/p2229, PIR reports include questionnaire-style assessments, timeline audit data, and configurable report templates that can incorporate PA data. Attachments (C) and key incident fields (D) may appear in the incident record but are not the specified PIR content types.

questions.stem: Security tag used when a piece of information requires support to be effectively acted upon, yet carries risks to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside of the organizations involved.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Traffic Light Protocol > TLP:AMBER: TLP:AMBER (B) is the security tag for information that requires support to be acted upon but carries risks to privacy, reputation, or operations if shared outside the organizations involved. Per p4273, TLP uses four colors for information sensitivity. TLP:GREEN (A) is for community-wide sharing. TLP:RED (C) is for named recipients only. TLP:WHITE (D) is for unrestricted public disclosure.

questions.stem: Which Table would be commonly used for Security Incident Response?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Tables > Security Incident Table: The sn_si_incident table (D) is commonly used for Security Incident Response. Per p2053: 'Table: Security Incident (sn_si_incident)' is referenced for response templates and quick messages. This is the primary SIR data table. sn_si_sec_incident (A) and sn_sir_incident (B) are not valid table names. The regular incident table (C) is for ITSM incidents, not security incidents.

questions.stem: ServiceNow follows the basic guidelines of the NIST lifecycle. Based on the best course of action, usually guided by runbooks and established procedures, problems sought to be fixed in which phase?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > NIST Lifecycle > Eradication Phase: Problems are sought to be fixed in the Eradication phase (C) of the NIST lifecycle. Eradication focuses on removing the root cause of the security incident — such as eliminating malware, closing vulnerabilities, and fixing exploited systems — guided by runbooks and established procedures. Analysis (A) determines the scope. Detection (B) identifies the incident. Review (D) occurs post-resolution.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the Security Incident Response Team?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Team Purpose > Handle Security Incidents: The main purpose of the Security Incident Response Team is to handle security incidents (C). The SIR Team manages the full lifecycle of security incidents from detection through containment, eradication, and recovery. Managing vulnerability response (A) is the Vulnerability Response team's purpose. Escalating incidents (B) is one activity, not the main purpose. Patching (D) is an IT operations task.

questions.stem: What are some of the recommended duties each SIR team should have?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Team Duties > All of the Above: Recommended SIR team duties include all of the above (D) — Coaching, Monitoring activities, and Testing. Coaching develops team capabilities, monitoring activities detects threats, and testing validates security controls and response procedures. All three are standard SIR team responsibilities.

questions.stem: Which role is needed to amend Security Incident Response Script Includes?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Script Includes > Required Role: The admin role (D) is required to amend Security Incident Response Script Includes. Script Includes are platform-level server-side scripts that require the system administrator role to modify. sn_si.admin (C) is a scoped admin for SIR configuration but does not have access to modify script includes without the platform admin role. script_admin (A) and activity_admin (B) are not standard ServiceNow roles.

questions.stem: Users can create and update security incidents, requests, and tasks, as well as problems, changes, and outages related to their incidents with which role?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Roles > sn_si.basic: Users with the sn_si.basic role can create and update security incidents, requests, and tasks, as well as problems, changes, and outages (D). This is the basic Security Incident access role underlying more advanced SIR roles. Per p1886, this foundational role provides the core access needed for incident creation and update activities. itil (A) is an ITSM role. sn_si.manager (B) has additional management capabilities. sn_si.ciso (C) is dashboard-focused.

questions.stem: The sn_si.external role is given to external users working on security incidents. What activities can external user complete with this role? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > External Role > Activities: Two activities external users can complete with the sn_si.external role are: View assigned Tasks (C) and Work Tasks assigned to them (D). Per p1887: 'Security Incident External [sn_si.external] - View any security incidents that belong to their particular group' — this scopes their access to tasks assigned within their group. Viewing related CI records (A) and unrestricted security incident viewing (B) exceed the external role's permissions.

questions.stem: What are the benefits of having an SIR Team? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Team Benefits > Three Benefits: Three benefits of having an SIR Team are: Reduced cost of recovery (A), Quicker incident resolutions (D), and Dedicated resources (E). A dedicated SIR team reduces recovery costs through faster, more effective responses, resolves incidents more quickly with specialized skills, and provides committed resources for security response. Increased headcount (B) is a cost, not a benefit. Reduced security incidents (C) is a prevention goal, not a response team benefit.

questions.stem: What measures activity outputs?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Metrics > Activity Outputs: Business metrics (A) measure activity outputs. Business metrics quantify what activities produce — such as number of incidents closed, mean time to respond, and cost per incident. Leading indicators (B) predict future performance. Lagging indicators (C) reflect historical outcomes. Business trends (D) show patterns over time but do not specifically measure activity outputs.

questions.stem: Which Security Incident Response product tiers offer baseline orchestration and automation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Product Tiers > Orchestration: Standard (A) and Professional (B) are the Security Incident Response product tiers that offer baseline orchestration and automation. These tiers include Integration Hub capabilities for connecting with third-party security tools and automating response workflows. Enterprise (C) may not be a distinct SIR tier. Basic (D) provides foundational features without advanced orchestration.

questions.stem: What are some of the ways SIR teams can increase their productivity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Productivity > Improvement Ways: Three ways SIR teams can increase productivity are: Process automation (A), Form personalization (B), and Training (C). Automation reduces manual effort, form personalization streamlines data entry and analyst workflows, and training improves analyst efficiency and effectiveness. Using spreadsheet pivot tables (D) is not a SIR productivity strategy. Hiring additional staff (E) increases cost rather than improving individual productivity.

questions.stem: What roles are required to modify Security Incident Catalog items?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Incident Catalog > Modification Roles: Modifying Security Incident Catalog items requires both the platform admin and sn_si.admin roles (C). Platform admin is needed for catalog administration at the system level, while sn_si.admin is needed for SIR-specific catalog configurations. sn_si.admin alone (A variant) lacks catalog admin rights. sn_si.analyst (B variants) cannot modify catalog items. sn_si.integration_user (D) is an integration-specific role.

questions.stem: When designing the Security Incident Catalog what should happen to all catalog items?

options.text: All catalog items should be displayed. These represent incidents common to all businesses.
All catalog items should be designed specifically to that customer's agreed needs.
All catalog items should be removed. They're just examples, and must be replaced by different ones specific to that customer.
All catalog items should be renamed to suit the language for that customer, so users know which to pick.

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Catalog Design > Customization: All catalog items should be designed specifically to that customer's agreed needs (B). The Security Incident Catalog should reflect the types of incidents relevant to that organization's environment and security policies. Displaying all default items (A) ignores customer context. Removing all items (C) would leave no starting point. Renaming only (D) is insufficient without redesigning for actual customer requirements.

questions.stem: Which of the following are required to allow inbound emails to be parsed into Security Incidents? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Email Parsing > Required Configuration: Three requirements to allow inbound emails to be parsed into Security Incidents are: Set Properties (A), Set Parsing Rules (B), and Set Field Transforms (C). Per p4253: properties configure email addresses for parsing. Parsing rules match incoming emails. Per p4266: field transforms map external values to ServiceNow field values. Assignment Rules (D) handle routing after creation. Business Rules (E) are for automation, not parsing setup.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are the target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MITRE ATT&CK > Target Personas: Three target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 are: Security and Threat Intelligence Administrators (A), Security Analysis (B), and SOC Managers and CISO (D). These are the security operations roles that use ATT&CK framework data for threat mapping, detection, and strategic oversight. IT Project Users (C) are not a security operations persona and do not use ATT&CK data in their workflows.

questions.stem: Rollup framework capability model configures linked records for what purpose?

options.text: Rollup Data Loss Prevention records to Major Security Incident
Rollup additional records information to Major Security Incident
Rollup additional records information to Data Loss Prevention Incidents
Rollup additional records information to imported Security Incidents

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Major Security Incident > Rollup Framework: The Rollup framework capability model configures linked records to rollup additional records information to the Major Security Incident (B). Per p2543: 'Create rollup record configuration to link and unlink additional records to MSI' — this enables consolidating related CIs, observables, and IOCs into the major security incident. This is not for DLP records (A, C) or imported security incidents (D).

questions.stem: Events within the platform that are utilized for the creation of Alerts and/or Security Incidents are held in which table?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Events > Storage Table: Events from external tools used for Alerts and Security Incident creation are held in the em_event table (C). Per p3153: 'Create ServiceNow Security Event: Events are stored in the em_event table. Note: Install Event Management plugin to access the em_event table.' sir_event (A) and sysevent (B) are not the correct table names. sys_event (D) is a different platform table for system events.

questions.stem: Security Incidents can be created using a manual UI Action on which one of the following record types?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Incident Creation > Manual UI Action: Security Incidents can be created using a manual UI Action on an Alert record (D). Alert records in Event Management have a 'Create Security Incident' UI action that allows analysts to manually escalate alerts to security incidents. Event records (A) may also support this, but Alert is the primary source. Email Notification (B) and Workflow (C) do not have a 'Create Security Incident' UI action.

questions.stem: Select the one capability that retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint.
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Capabilities > Get Network Statistics: Get Network Statistics (F) retrieves a list of active network connections from a host or endpoint. Per p4291: 'Get Network Statistics: Retrieves a list of active network connections from an endpoint or host. This capability is used for incident enrichment during investigations.' Get Running Processes (C) retrieves processes. Isolate Host (E) restricts connections. Sightings Search (A), Block Action (B), and Publish Watchlist (D) are different capabilities.

questions.stem: LDAP, Direct Web Service, and SOAP are types of what?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Integrations > Types: LDAP, Direct Web Service, and SOAP are types of integration methods (A). These are different technical protocols used to integrate ServiceNow with external systems for data exchange. Data mapping (B) is the process of aligning fields between systems. ServiceNow access protocol (C) and Reporting methods (D) are not the category these three belong to.

questions.stem: Events received from external tools should include what information? (Choose three.)

options.text: A list of similar indicators that were discovered in the event details
Event description, which populates the description of the security incident
Event classification set to Security to distinguish them from other IT events
Node set to the name, IP address, or sys_id of the CI that becomes the affected resource

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Event Ingestion > Required Information: Three pieces of information events from external tools should include are: Event description (B) to populate the security incident description, Event classification set to Security (C) to distinguish from IT events, and Node set to CI name/IP/sys_id (E) to identify the affected resource. Per p3153, these fields map to security incident fields. Similar indicators (A) and whitelisted/blacklisted IPs (D) are not required event fields.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. (Choose three.)

options.text: Perform host enrichment actions to gather more information about the endpoint, which includes host details, logged-in users, and observable related machines details.
Find indicators of compromise (IoC) and enrich security incidents with threat intelligence data.
Perform Enterprise Security Search to sight potential malicious observables across endpoints, and take remediation actions.
Perform response actions such as Isolate host, Remove isolation, Restrict app execution, Run antivirus scan, Remove app restriction, and Stop and quarantine file.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Microsoft Defender > Key Features: Three key features of Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration are: Host enrichment (A), IoC enrichment (B), and Response actions (D). Per the SIR doc, the Defender integration enriches security incidents with host and IoC data and enables response actions like isolating endpoints. Enterprise Security Search (C) is a separate integration capability, not a key feature of the Defender integration.

questions.stem: The time zone of a CI is determined by:

options.text: The time zone setting on the computer
The time zone field on the Clock
The time zone of the asset owner
The time zone of the location

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Configuration Items > Timezone: The timezone of a CI is derived from its Location (D). In ServiceNow, Configuration Items inherit timezone from the Location record associated with them. This allows SIR to correctly timestamp events and incidents based on where the affected asset is located. Timezone is not stored directly on the CI itself (A), nor from the assigned user (B) or the incident record (C).

questions.stem: Security tags can be applied to which of the following record types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Security Tags > Application: Security tags in SIR can be applied to Indicators/Observables (C), Response Tasks (D), and Security Incidents (E). These three record types support tag classification for information sharing controls like TLP. Alerts (A) and Configuration Items (B) do not support security tags in the baseline SIR application.

questions.stem: The creation of custom process definitions would require which of the following platform components? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Process Definitions > Custom Components: To create a custom process definition, you need a Process Definition record (B) and a Script Include (D). The Process Definition record defines the lifecycle states and transitions, while the Script Include contains the server-side logic that drives state management for the custom process. A Flow (A) is optional for automation. A UI Policy (C) is for form behavior, not process definition.

questions.stem: Which Security tag is used when information is useful for the awareness of all participating organizations as well as with peers within the broader community or sector?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Traffic Light Protocol > TLP:GREEN: TLP:GREEN (D) is used for information that is useful for awareness by the wider community. Per p4273, TLP:GREEN information may be shared with peers and partner organizations but not posted publicly. TLP:WHITE (A) is for unrestricted public sharing. TLP:AMBER (B) requires need-to-know restrictions. TLP:RED (C) is for named recipients only.

questions.stem: Which of the following management activities are associated with Major Security Incident Management?

options.text: Link security incidents as child incidents to other child incidents, so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as parent incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as child incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked
Link security incidents as minor incidents to the major security incident (MSI) so that all security incidents can be worked

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MSIM > Key Activity: The key activity of Major Security Incident Management is linking child security incidents to a major security incident (C). MSIM consolidates related security incidents under a single major incident for coordinated response. Creating problem records (A) is ITSM. Assigning severity levels (B) is part of general SIR triage. Generating compliance reports (D) is a governance function.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of Major Security Incident Management. (Choose three.)

options.text: Organize response tasks across multiple parent security incidents
Chat channel manager and activity stream components to manage communications across multiple security, IT, and functional groups via a Microsoft Teams integration
Organize response tasks across multiple 'child' security incidents
Dedicated workspace for managing major security incidents specifically designed for the major security incident manager user role

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MSIM > Key Features: Three key features of Major Security Incident Management are: Dedicated chat channel (B), Child response tasks (C), and Dedicated MSIM workspace (D). These features enable coordinated response by providing a collaboration channel, task management for sub-incidents, and a purpose-built workspace for major incident handling. Automated root cause analysis (A) is not a baseline MSIM feature.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of the Malware Information Sharing Platform. (Choose three.)

options.text: Dedicated workspace for managing major security incidents specifically designed for the major security incident manager user role
Auto-extract MITRE-ATT&CKTM information from MISP attributes and associate the information to SIR security incidents.
Add security incident associated observables as attributes to a MISP event.
Update a MISP event from SIR which includes adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes.

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MISP Integration > Key Features: Three key features of the MISP integration are: Auto-extract MITRE ATT&CK techniques (B), Add observables as MISP attributes (C), and Update MISP events from security incidents (D). These enable bidirectional threat intelligence sharing between ServiceNow SIR and MISP. Automated incident creation from MISP alerts (A) is not a listed MISP integration feature.

questions.stem: Which role must a user have to customize major security incident reports based on the incremental progress since last summary update?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MSI Reports > Required Role: The sn_msi.workspace_manager role (B) is required to customize Major Security Incident reports. This role provides management access to the MSIM workspace configuration including report customization. sn_si.admin (A) manages SIR configuration but not MSIM report customization specifically. sn_si.manager (C) has incident management capabilities. admin (D) has broad access but is not the minimum required role.

questions.stem: Which statement about Security Incident Calculators is correct?

options.text: All Calculator Groups run in order but only the calculator with the highest order in that group runs
All Calculator Groups run in order but only the first matching calculator from each group will apply
All Calculator Groups run in order but only the first matching group will apply
All Calculator Groups run in order and all calculators in the first matching group apply

questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Severity Calculator > Group Behavior: All calculator groups run, but only the first matching calculator within each group applies to determine severity (B). Calculator groups allow multiple calculators to be evaluated in priority order, with the first matching one in the group setting the severity contribution. Not all calculators run without restriction (A). Groups do not prevent all calculators from running (C). The highest-scored calculator does not automatically win (D).

questions.stem: When a Post-Incident Review report is created, it can be found…

options.text: as a published article in a knowledge base
as an unpublished article in a knowledge base
as an attachment to the original security incident
as an article pending approval in a knowledge base

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Post Incident Review > Report Location: The PIR report is generated as an attachment on the original security incident (C). Per p2223/p2229, the Post Incident Review report is attached directly to the security incident record after completion. It is not stored in a separate PIR table (A), a dedicated report module (B), or a knowledge article (D).

questions.stem: What is the main goal of the Security Incident Response process?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Main Goal > Reduce Time: The main goal of Security Incident Response is to reduce the time to contain security incidents (B). SIR focuses on accelerating containment to limit the blast radius of security events. Reducing the number of incidents (A) is a prevention goal. Improving compliance posture (C) is a governance objective. Automating all security tasks (D) is a means, not the primary goal.

questions.stem: What should you consider before helping customers automate different processes?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Automation > Key Consideration: The most important consideration before automating processes is understanding the customer's willingness to change (A). Automation requires organizational buy-in and process maturity; without stakeholder acceptance, automation initiatives will fail regardless of technical capability. Available integrations (B) and tool availability (C) are secondary. Cost savings (D) are a benefit, not a primary consideration.

questions.stem: Security Incidents can be created using which platform functionality?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Platform Functionality > Incident Creation: Inbound Email Actions (A) is the platform functionality used to create security incidents from incoming emails. Inbound Email Actions process incoming emails and trigger record creation based on configured rules. Business Rules (B) trigger on database operations. Flow Designer (C) automates workflows after records exist. UI Actions (D) are triggered by user interaction on forms.

questions.stem: Which platform functionality uses Conditions and Scripts to take action on a target table when receiving emails?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Inbound Email Actions > Components: Inbound Email Actions use Conditions and Scripts (B) to process incoming emails. Conditions determine whether an action applies to a given email, and scripts define what happens when conditions are met — such as creating a security incident. Triggers and Actions (A) are Flow Designer components. Rules and Transforms (C) are used in email parsing configuration. Filters and Workflows (D) are not the primary IEA components.

questions.stem: Actions packaged in Scoped applications are called:
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Scoped Applications > Spokes: In scoped applications, actions are called Spokes (C). Integration Hub Spokes are pre-built integration packages that provide reusable actions for connecting ServiceNow with external systems within scoped application flows. Scripts (A) are server-side code. Flows (B) are the automated process containers. Subflows (D) are reusable flow components, not the scoped action packages.

questions.stem: When testing a flow, the action outcomes can be found where?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Test Outcomes: Execution Details (C) in Flow Designer shows the outcomes when testing a flow. The Execution Details panel displays step-by-step results, inputs, outputs, and any errors for each action when a flow is tested or executed. Flow Summary (A) shows high-level information. Audit Log (B) tracks changes to records. Test Results (D) is not the specific panel name in Flow Designer.

questions.stem: Flow Logic in the baseline includes: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Logic > Baseline Components: The two baseline Flow Logic components are For Each Loops (A) and If/Then conditions (C). Flow Logic provides conditional branching and iteration within flows. For Each loops iterate over collections of records, and If/Then conditions branch flow execution based on criteria. While loops (B) are not a baseline Flow Logic component. Try/Catch blocks (D) are scripting constructs, not Flow Logic components.

questions.stem: What contains a set of reusable operations that are designed to be used in multiple playbooks?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Reusable Operations: Subflows (D) are the reusable operations that can be invoked from multiple playbooks or flows. Subflows encapsulate common sequences of actions that can be called from different parent flows, enabling reuse across SIR playbooks. Actions (A) are individual steps within flows. Spokes (B) are integration action packages. Workflows (C) are the legacy automation engine.

questions.stem: What automates processes and supports triggers with a sequence of reusable actions?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Definition: Flows (C) automate processes and support triggers with a sequence of reusable actions in Flow Designer. A flow is triggered by a defined event or condition and executes a sequence of actions to automate a business process. Subflows (A) are reusable components called by flows, not triggered independently. Actions (B) are individual steps. Spokes (D) are integration packages, not process automation containers.

questions.stem: Once a Phishing Email record is created, which Flow creates a new Security Incident record?

options.text: Transform Phishing Email to Security Incident

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Phishing > Transform Flow: The 'Transform Phishing Email to Security Incident' flow (D) creates a new Security Incident record once a Phishing Email record is created. Per p2138: 'The Transform user-reported phishing emails to security incidents flow creates security incidents from the phishing email records and aggregates similar records into a single incident.' The other options (A, B, C) are not the correct flow names.

questions.stem: When an inbound email is processed and identified as a phishing email what table is it stored in for URP v2?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > User Reported Phishing > Storage Table: When an inbound email is processed as a phishing email in URP v2, it is stored in the Security Incident Phishing Email table (B), corresponding to sn_si_phishing_email. Per p2141/p2143: 'When a new phishing email record is created in the sn_si_phishing_email table.' Security Incident Alert (A) and Security Incident (C) are different tables. Incident (D) is the ITSM table.

questions.stem: In order to use User Reported Phishing v2, what must occur in Flow Designer?

options.text: Phishing Email Aggregation Subflow must be activated
Transform Flow must be copied and activated

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > User Reported Phishing > Flow Designer Requirement: To use URP v2, the Transform Flow must be copied and activated (E) in Flow Designer. Per p2151: 'select Activate to activate the flow so that it can be executed.' The flow must be copied from the baseline template and then activated — simply publishing (A) or activating without copying (B) is insufficient. Transform Action (C) and Aggregation Subflow (D) are not the correct requirements.

questions.stem: When setting up a Playbook what field in the Flow Action for Creating a Response Task must contain the same value as the Runbook name?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Playbook > Runbook Name Match: The Short Description field (A) in the Flow Action for Creating a Response Task must contain the same value as the Runbook name. Per p2257: 'This is the short description of the task and you need this text (exactly as it appears in the playbook) to associate a knowledge article with the task.' Action (B), Runbook (C), and Knowledge article (D) are not the field that must match the runbook name.

questions.stem: Runbook records utilize a link to what type record for content?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Runbooks > Content Link: Runbook records link to Knowledge articles (A) for content. Per p1916: 'A runbook is an association between a published knowledge article and a specific task.' Per p2220: 'you can organize knowledge articles into runbooks, which create associations between the articles and specific tasks.' Response Tasks (B), Managed Documents (C), and Instruction Details (D) are not what runbooks link to for content.

questions.stem: In a Flow, if the Create Response Task set Incident state V1 action is selected, what field contains the yes_no value that drives a question being asked in the playbook?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Playbook Question Driver: The Outcome Type field (B) contains the yes_no value that drives a question being asked in the playbook when the 'Create Response Task set Incident state V1' action is selected. The Outcome Type field on a response task determines whether a decision point (yes/no question) is presented to the analyst. Question Type (A), SI State (C), and Answer Type (D) are not the field driving yes/no questions.

questions.stem: Runbooks are used to create a relationship between what components? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Runbooks > Relationship Components: Runbooks create a relationship between Security Incident Response Tasks (B) and Knowledge articles (F). Per p1916: 'A runbook is an association between a published knowledge article and a specific task.' Per p2220, this enables knowledge articles to open automatically while working response tasks. Events (A), Alerts (D), and Workflow Triggers (E) are not components of a runbook relationship.

questions.stem: What is included in the real-time data model in the right pane of the Flow Designer UI that may be dragged and dropped into fields in the main flow workspace?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Flow Designer > Data Model: Data Pills (C) are included in the real-time data model in the right pane of the Flow Designer UI and can be dragged and dropped into fields in the main flow workspace. Data pills represent dynamic field values from trigger outputs and action outputs. Record Objects (A), Table References (B), and Code Snippets (D) are not the draggable elements in the Flow Designer data model pane.

questions.stem: What kind of rules can be used to configure how email phishing incidents are processed? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Phishing Email > Processing Rules: Ingestion Rules (D) and Duplication Rules (F) configure how email phishing incidents are processed. Per p2141, ingestion/email matching rules determine which emails create phishing records. Duplication Rules configure aggregation of similar phishing records into a single incident per p2138. Risk Rules (A), Inbound Property Rules (B), CI Lookup Rules (C), and Condition Rules (E) are not phishing processing rule types.

questions.stem: Which role must a user have to customize major security incident reports based on the incremental progress since last summary update?
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MSIM > Report Customization Role: The sn_msi.workspace_manager role (D) is required to customize major security incident reports. Per p2409: 'MSI Manager sn_msi.workspace_manager — View and edit incident record data... Promote the security incident to a major security incident.' Per p2541, this is the manager-level MSIM role. sn_msi.workspace_user (A) and sn_msi.workspace_responder (B) have limited access. sn_msim.workspace_responder (C) is not a valid role name.

questions.stem: Risk Score weighting uses which of the following components? (Choose two.)

options.text: Business impact of a CI or Security Incident
Severity and Priority of a Security incident
Cost and Risk of an affected service
SLA and Schedule of an impacted service
Impact and Urgency of a Security incident

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Risk Score > Weighting Components: Risk Score weighting uses Business Impact of a CI or Security Incident (A) and Severity and Priority of a Security Incident (B). Per p1914: 'if a security incident has a Business impact set to 2-High and a Priority set to 3-Moderate, the respective weights in the Risk Score Weights table are looked up' to compute the risk score. Cost/Risk (C), SLA/Schedule (D), and Impact/Urgency (E) are not the Risk Score weighting components.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for identifying security incidents?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Incident Identification > Responsibility: Everyone (A) is responsible for identifying security incidents. This is a foundational security principle — all employees, not just security staff, can encounter and must report potential security incidents. Limiting identification responsibility to Managers (B), IT personnel (C), or Security analysts (D) alone would leave significant detection gaps in the organization.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are key features of the Malware Information Sharing Platform (Choose three.)

options.text: Dedicated MISP workspace for managing major security incidents
Auto-extract MITRE-ATT&CK™ information from MISP attributes and associate them to SIR security incidents
Attribute enrichment including adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes
Send malware to MISP for detonation
Add security incident associated observables as attributes to a MISP event

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MISP > Key Features: Three key features of MISP integration are: Auto-extract MITRE ATT&CK information from MISP attributes (B), Attribute enrichment including adding or updating tags, galaxies, or attributes (C), and Add security incident observables as attributes to a MISP event (E). Per p3484: these are explicitly listed MISP integration features. Dedicated MISP workspace (A) is not a feature. Sending malware for detonation (D) is not a MISP integration capability.

questions.stem: Select all of the following which are the target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 > Target Personas: The three target personas for MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 are: SOC Managers and CISO (A), Security and Threat Intelligence Administrators (B), and Security Analysts (C). Per p3406/p3465, these roles use the ATT&CK repository for strategic oversight, administration, and operational analysis respectively. Compliance Managers (D) and Penetration Testers (E) are not MITRE ATT&CK 2.0 target personas in SIR.

questions.stem: How does a user modify Risk Scores to suit their organizational needs?

options.text: alter values in the Risk Score Configuration module
amend constants in the RiskScoreUtil script include
change the business impact for affected Business Services and Configuration Items
recode logic in the Risk Score Calculator

questions.explanation: [Zurich] SIR > Risk Score > Modification: A user modifies Risk Scores to suit organizational needs by altering values in the Risk Score Configuration module (A). Per p1914, the Risk Score Weights table stores the weight values for Business Impact and Priority fields — these are configured via the Risk Score Configuration module. Amending script constants (B), changing CI business impact (C), and recoding calculator logic (D) are not the standard way to adjust risk score weights.

questions.stem: What are some of the ways SIR teams can increase their productivity? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Productivity > Improvement Ways: Three ways SIR teams can increase productivity are: Process automation (C), Training (D), and Form personalization (E). Per p1875, automation reduces manual effort; training improves analyst efficiency; form personalization streamlines workflows. Red/Blue automation (A) is a security testing concept, not a SIR productivity strategy. Export to spreadsheet pivot tables (B) is not a recommended SIR productivity approach.

questions.stem: What is one of the Security Incident Response Team’s activities?
questions.explanation: [Platform] SIR > Team Activities > Monitoring: One of the Security Incident Response Team's key activities is monitoring security alerts (C). The SIR team monitors alerts and events from security tools to detect and respond to incidents. Patching vulnerabilities (A) is an IT operations task. Escalating incidents (B) is one step, not a primary team activity. Penetration testing (D) is an offensive security activity performed by red teams.
